terminal.description: A shell in your workspace. Run the hut's rules here, and try your classes from main.

tasks.title: Write NoRoomException, which says how many seats are free
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 1`, write a class `NoRoomException`, a checked exception, with a constructor `NoRoomException(String boat, int seatsFree)`. Its message names the boat and the seats free, as in `No room on Linnet: 2 seats free`, and a method `int seatsFree()` gives back the seats free.

Check makes, throws and catches `NoRoomException`s of its own, two at once included, keeps one in a variable of type `Exception`, and reads `getMessage()` and `seatsFree()`. It also compiles a method of its own that throws one with no `throws`, which must be refused because the exception is checked.
nextSteps: Read the part of the lesson about a class that extends Exception.
Write the first line of the class, with the exception class it extends.
Write the field, then the constructor: its first line hands the message on, its second keeps the seats free.
Write seatsFree(), and take the // off the first lines in main.
hints: Which class it extends decides whether it is checked. The lesson shows both.
getMessage() gives back the message that was handed to Exception's constructor, and that hand-over has to be the first line of yours.
The constructor: `super("No room on " + boat + ": " + seatsFree + " seats free");`, then `this.seatsFree = seatsFree;`.

tasks.title: Throw it when a boat is full, and catch it by its name
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 2`, write a class `Booking` with two methods.

`static String reserve(String boat, int free, int wanted)` gives back `Booked 3 on Linnet`, with the places wanted and the boat. Fewer than 1 place wanted is refused with an `IllegalArgumentException` whose message names the places. More places than are free throws a `NoRoomException` for that boat with the seats free.

`static String answer(String boat, int free, int wanted)` gives back what `reserve` gives back, or, when there is no room, `Only 2 left on Linnet`, with the seats free that the exception holds. A caller of `answer` needs no `try`, and fewer than 1 place still reaches the caller.

Check runs your class beside a `NoRoomException` of its own, written as Task 1 asks but with words of its own in its message, so this task is judged on its own lines. It calls both methods with boats of its own, catches the `NoRoomException` by its name and reads the seats free it holds, and compiles a call of `reserve` with no `try`, which must be refused, and a call of `answer` with no `try`, which must be accepted.
nextSteps: Read the part of the lesson about catching an exception by its own name.
Write reserve: refuse fewer than 1 place, then throw a NoRoomException when there is no room, then give back the booked line.
Give reserve's first line the throws the compiler asks for.
Write answer with a catch for the one exception a full boat brings, and build its line with the seats free the exception holds.
hints: NoRoomException is checked, so reserve says it may throw it, and answer either catches it or says so too. The task says a caller of answer needs no try.
A catch for Exception would catch the IllegalArgumentException as well, and could not call seatsFree(). Catch the exception by its own name.
In answer: `try { return reserve(boat, free, wanted); } catch (NoRoomException e) { return "Only " + e.seatsFree() + " left on " + boat; }`.

docs.title: Specifying the exceptions thrown by a method

tasks.title: Wrap a bad ledger line, and keep the cause
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 3`, write a class `BadLineException`, a checked exception, with a constructor `BadLineException(String line, Throwable cause)`: its message names the line, and it keeps the cause. Then write a class `Lines` with a method `static int seatsOn(String line)`, for ledger lines such as `09:00,Linnet,9`. It gives back the seats, the third part. When the line has no third part, or it is not a whole number, it throws a `BadLineException` for the line, with the exception Java threw as its cause. A `null` line is a mistake in the calling code: its exception must reach the caller as it is.

Check makes a `BadLineException` with a cause of its own and reads `getCause()` and `getMessage()`. It calls `seatsOn` with lines of its own, good, with a word for the seats, with no seats at all, and `null`, catches the `BadLineException` by its name, and reads which exception is its cause. It also compiles a call of `seatsOn` with no `try`, which must be refused.
nextSteps: Read the part of the lesson about keeping the cause.
Write BadLineException: its constructor hands both the message and the cause to Exception.
Write seatsOn: split the line, and read the third part inside a try.
Catch the two exceptions a bad line brings, and throw a BadLineException with each as its cause.
hints: Exception has a constructor that takes a message and a cause. A line with two parts brings one exception, a word for the seats another.
Splitting a null line fails before any try, which is what the task asks. Inside the try, catch only what a bad line brings, and throw your own exception with the caught one handed over.
The constructor: `super("Bad ledger line: " + line, cause);`. In seatsOn: `catch (NumberFormatException | ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException e) { throw new BadLineException(line, e); }`.
